title: A carillon’s tower bells are played with the fists and feet

cover.alt: Close-up of a carillonneur’s arms at the carillon keyboard in St. Rumbold’s Cathedral, Mechelen: rows of wooden baton keys below a stand of sheet music.
cover.credit: Rudi Van Poele (video), Jasper Depraetere (playing) · CC BY 3.0

body: A carillon is a set of at least 23 tuned bells, played from a keyboard of wooden batons up in the tower. The player presses each key down with a **closed fist**, and the lowest one-and-a-half to two-and-a-half octaves are also linked to pedals played with the feet. The modern instrument dates from 1644, when Jacob van Eyck and the Hemony brothers cast the first tuned carillon, and about 700 exist today, most of them in and around the Low Countries.

slides.alt: Close-up of a carillon keyboard: two rows of wooden batons below a stand of sheet music, as the player’s arms move along them and press the keys down with closed fists.
slides.caption: In the tower of St. Rumbold’s Cathedral in Mechelen, Belgium, a carillonneur plays a prelude by pressing the wooden batons down with his fists.
slides.credit: Rudi Van Poele (video), Jasper Depraetere (playing) · CC BY 3.0 · excerpt
slides.music: “Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.heading: How many bells make a carillon
slides.note: With fewer than 23 bells, the instrument is called a chime. Two carillons share the 77-bell record.

slides.heading: The tower in the clip
slides.text: Jef Denyn, a leading figure in the carillon’s revival, played the carillon of St. Rumbold’s Cathedral in Mechelen, Belgium, and drew worldwide interest to the instrument. In 1922 a carillon school opened in Mechelen with Denyn as its first director.

slides.heading: Oldest first
items: The first tuned carillon is cast
A carillon school opens in Mechelen
slides.explanation: Oudenaarde’s town hall had a primitive carillon in 1510, the first tuned carillon was cast in 1644, and Mechelen’s school opened in 1922.

slides.prompt: Bell founders tune more than a bell’s main note. Which overtone gives carillons their character?
slides.answer: A minor third, called the tierce
slides.detail: Founders tune five principal tones in each bell, most notably the minor third overtone called the tierce, which gives rise to the unique sound of carillons.
